name: Bernardo Faria Pressure System
description: Compare Bernardo Faria’s over/under-centered No Gi Pressure Passing with a broader guard-passing course, then choose an entry and troubleshooting topic.
summary: Study over/under entries and defensive reactions through Bernardo Faria’s No Gi Pressure Passing.
overview: No Gi Pressure Passing by Bernardo Faria concentrates first on entering and troubleshooting the over/under. Later sections widen the study to other pressure passes and positional follow-ups. Treat those as separate topics to investigate, not an automatic chain.

products.title: No Gi Pressure Passing
products.blurb: Study over/under entries and defensive reactions through Bernardo Faria’s No Gi Pressure Passing.
products.best_for: You want to investigate why an over/under attempt stalls at entry or after an opponent’s response.
products.study_focus: Start with Volume 1’s mechanics chapter; distinguish the entry sections from Volume 2’s troubleshooting.

fits: You want to investigate why an over/under attempt stalls at entry or after an opponent’s response.
consider_alternative_if: For broader coverage of split squat, half butterfly and leg-entanglement positions, compare Gordon Ryan’s Systematically Attacking The Guard.

includes: Entries from open, closed, butterfly and knee-shield guards.
Troubleshooting hip escapes, leg hooks and submission threats.
Later double-under, folding and half-guard passing topics.
limits: The course adapts pressure passing to no-gi; it does not provide a dedicated gi collar-and-sleeve passing curriculum.

start_here.title: Separate an entry problem from a response problem
start_here.task: Read the free outline and make two headings: reaching over/under and responding once there. Place one chapter relevant to your recent passing difficulty under each. If you have course access, start with the mechanics chapter before studying your selected response.
